reviews.title: A complete failure for Rawdah booking!
reviews.text:
This app has completely failed at the one thing it is supposed to do.

My entire family tried repeatedly to book a Rawdah permit before arriving in Madinah and throughout our stay. We refreshed the app countless times, installed the latest update, and still couldn’t secure a single booking.

We even went to the official Nusuk help desk, where we were told to wait for the new app update and try again. We did exactly that, and nothing changed.

This app hasn’t made access to Rawdah easier, it has just created another barrier for pilgrims. People travel thousands of miles and spend a great deal of money, only to be left endlessly refreshing an app with no transparency or realistic chance of getting a permit.

We were in Madinah this week, so don’t assume the TikTok videos claiming it’s easy to book Rawdah reflect everyone’s experience. They certainly didn’t reflect ours.

Pilgrims deserve a booking system that actually works.

reviews.title: This app gets worse and worse day by day.
reviews.text:
Using this app to try and book a Rawdah visit and Itikaf slot has been an incredibly frustrating experience. Since the app is the only way to access bookings, you would expect it to work reliably — but unfortunately, that hasn’t been the case at all.

Most of the time the app simply shows “soon,” “maintenance,” or other messages that prevent you from booking anything. On the rare occasions when bookings do open, it seems to last for barely a minute before everything is gone again.

Even basic functionality is unreliable. At times it’s impossible to log in, verification codes don’t arrive, and sometimes the app claims that your ID is already registered and refuses to let you proceed. These kinds of technical problems make an already limited booking system even more difficult to navigate.

What makes the situation even more disappointing is that this is an official system from one of the wealthiest countries in the world, responsible for managing access to one of the most sacred places in Islam. With that level of resources and responsibility, you would expect a much more stable, accessible, and well-designed platform.

This is the official platform of the Saudi government for pilgrims, yet when someone needs support, there is absolutely no response. No communication. No guidance. Nothing.

For a system that manages essential services for visitors, this level of neglect is unacceptable. Pilgrims deserve proper support, not silence.

reviews.title: Deeply Disappointing Experience with Nusuk App and Staff Conduct
reviews.text:
Our family is extremely disappointed with the Nusuk app and the overall experience surrounding it. The app is poorly designed and urgently requires major improvements. It fails to display the full Umrah itinerary, leaving us confused about our schedule. When attempting to book Rawdah time slots, the app immediately shows everything as “full” right after selecting a time, and it does not even allow us to download the appointment properly.

The flight-booking feature is also inadequate, as it only displays domestic flight options instead of international ones, which is completely impractical for pilgrims travelling from abroad.

Even more upsetting than the technical issues was the behaviour of the staff. We booked our Umrah permit through the app, yet when we showed it at the entrance, the security personnel shouted at us, telling us there was no need for it. This could have easily been communicated politely and respectfully. Instead, we were spoken to harshly for simply following the instructions provided by the app.

Throughout our experience, neither Nusuk staff nor security personnel offered helpful guidance. The moment they realised we only speak English, their attitude became even more rude and dismissive. Several staff members shouted at us and told us to “find someone else” instead of providing support. This behaviour is unacceptable, especially in a place where pilgrims come seeking peace, respect, and spiritual comfort.
